name: club
style: Instrumental-only minimal club track in A minor at 110 BPM, centered on a rigid four-on-the-floor kick and a late, elastic bass as the main rhythmic fingerprint. The dry, unwavering kick is a cold mechanical ruler the plucky synthetic bass plays just behind, with quick decay, subtle slides and restrained filter moves to keep the groove playful yet detached. Tight off-beat closed hats and a lean, mostly straight top loop lightly embellish the grid, while sparse mid-high metallic stabs strike in select gaps as icy exclamation marks, never becoming a melody or eclipsing the bass. A small, dry clap or soft digital snare on 2 and 4 provides a low-key backbeat, and quiet FX plus rare one-note blips only mark transitions and hint at A minor as static harmony, no pads, chords or warmth, keeps focus on micro-timing, automation and the contrast of rigid drums, rubbery bass and precise metallic hits, leaving vocal-ready space but no voice-like sounds.
section:
[Intro]
(Start with only the rigid four-on-the-floor kick and very tight off-beat closed hats, dry and mechanical. Fade in a low-passed, simplified version of the elastic bass pattern, with fewer notes and less sub, entering a bit late against the kick to hint at the rubbery feel. Keep the room very empty, no metallic stabs yet, just a distant, short noise swell at the end of every 4 bars to mark phrases.)
[Instrumental Verse 1]
(Open the bass filter and reveal the full late, elastic groove as the clear center, still in a narrow A minor range. Add a very low, dry clap on 2 and 4 and keep the hats steady with occasional extra 16th-note ticks to underline the grid. Introduce sparse metallic stabs in select gaps after the bass phrases, no more than once every couple of bars, so each hit feels like a sharp, icy accent rather than a riff. FX stay minimal and quiet to keep the focus on the bass–kick tension.)
[Instrumental Hook 1]
(Intensify the bass line with a slightly busier syncopation, a few extra late notes and subtle pitch slides, keeping the same harmonic area. Push the hats a bit brighter and let the clap step forward just a little in level. Use metallic stabs more frequently, accenting most bars on off-beats or bar-ends, always leaving short pockets of silence around them. Drop in occasional short digital zaps or reversed hits at 8-bar turns to lift the energy while keeping the texture cold and minimal.)
[Instrumental Bridge 1]
(Pull the energy back by muting the clap and most metallic stabs, thinning the hats down to simple off-beats or even half-time for a few bars. Gently low-pass the bass and simplify its rhythm, leaving more air between notes while keeping the late feel. For one brief 1–2-bar moment, cut the kick entirely and let a filtered top loop and a single, slightly longer metallic tone or resonant stab imply the grid, then snap the kick back in to rebuild tension. Use a couple of more noticeable but still short FX swells to stretch the space without adding warmth.)
[Instrumental Hook 2]
(Return to the fullest version of the groove: strong, steady kick, regular hats, clap back on 2 and 4, and the most engaging elastic bass pattern from earlier, with tiny rhythmic variations and automation for movement. Let metallic stabs be at their most active, punctuating many gaps but never turning into a continuous line. Add a few extremely sparse one-note synth blips in the mid-high range (single A or E) answering some bass rests every 4–8 bars to enhance the playful edge. Maintain a clean, minimal mix so the rhythm and micro-timing feel like the peak rather than sheer loudness.)
[Outro]
Gradually strip elements away: first stop the one-note blips and metallic stabs, then pull the clap out and thin the hats until only a faint top click remains. Gently filter and reduce the complexity of the bass pattern, letting it feel more rigid and less elastic, while the kick continues its four-on-the-floor pulse for most of the outro. In the final bars, either fade the kick or filter it down, leaving a decaying, bit-crushed bass tail and a last soft noise sweep to end on an icy, empty space.)

name: trap
style: Instrumental-only dark trap type beat at 110 BPM in A minor, built around a heavy half-time pocket and a hypnotic low 808/sub riff as the primary hook. The fused 808–kick layer plays a simple, menacing A–G–E motif with occasional glides, locked to a solid snare/clap on beat 3 so the groove feels slow, weighty, and inevitable, with an optional short kick transient reinforcing main onsets without adding rhythmic busyness. Hi-hats are dry, crisp, and restrained, mostly 1/8 notes with light velocity shaping and brief 1/16–1/32 rolls used sparingly for subtle motion. A cold mid-range synth adds ominous off-beat stabs and dyads around A minor that color harmony without competing with the bass, while a very low, reverb-heavy pad or noise bed holds long, nearly static tones moving gently via filter changes. Sparse, dark FX hits and swells mark transitions, and the mix stays spacious with midrange reserved for a potential vocal, keeping upper layers minimal and cold so the identity remains the interaction between the sub-heavy riff and disciplined half-time drums in a relentlessly dark, tense atmosphere.
section:
[Intro]
(Start with only the distant ambient pad, low-passed and drenched in reverb to establish cold space. After one bar, fade in a filtered, thinned version of the 808-bass riff outlining A minor, without full sub weight, playing a simple A–G–E motif every 2 bars. Add a few very soft, sporadic closed-hat ticks on off-beats in the last bar before the verse to hint at the coming groove, but keep all drums and synth stabs otherwise absent.)
[Instrumental Verse 1]
.Drop
(Bring in the full half-time drum pocket and the main fused 808/sub motif: long, saturated hits on A–G–E locked tightly with a short, thumpy kick layer. Place a gritty snare/clap on beat 3 each bar. Run a restrained 1/8-note closed-hat pattern with light velocity variation and only rare, 1/16-note two-step rolls at the ends of 4-bar phrases. Introduce the ominous mid synth as very sparse, low-velocity stabs on off-beats every 2 bars, while the ambient pad sits low and static. Maintain clear space in the mids so the focus stays on the bass–drums pocket, as if leaving room for a future vocal.)
[Instrumental Hook 1]
(Elevate energy by making the 808-bass rhythm a touch more active: add a few extra anticipations before the snare while keeping the motif loopable over 4 bars. Keep the same snare and kick sound but slightly tighten their dynamics. Let the hats keep the 1/8-note base while adding brief 1/16 or 1/32 flurries leading into some snares, plus a couple of subtle off-beat openings. Have the mid synth stabs appear every bar now, occasionally holding through beat 3 to glue into the snare, and gently open the pad filter for a bit more airy hiss. Avoid any new lead lines so the hook still feels like a heavier, more insistent version of the verse.)
[Instrumental Bridge 1]
(Drop the hats entirely for the first 2 bars, leaving only kick, snare, 808-bass, and the distant pad to create a hollow, suspended feeling. Simplify the 808 line to mostly sustained A with the occasional G, using fewer glides and more legato holds so the groove feels slower and heavier. Either mute the mid synth stabs or let a single, very washed-out stab ring out once every 4 bars, pushed far back in reverb. Introduce one unique dark FX element, like a reversed metallic hit or sub drop, in the last bar as a quiet cue that Hook 2 is approaching, without brightening the spectrum.)
[Instrumental Hook 2]
(Bring back the full Hook 1 arrangement as the baseline: active 808 motif, full hats, mid synth stabs, and opened pad. Add a bit more micro-variation by inserting one extra syncopated 808 hit or short glide near the end of every 4-bar phrase and a few more targeted hat rolls into key snares, while keeping overall density restrained. Let the mid synth occasionally sustain a note across two beats between stabs to make this hook feel slightly fuller than Hook 1, but never evolve into a singable top melody. Maintain the same dark, tense harmony and avoid any harmonic resolution.)
[Outro]
(Gradually strip elements away over the last 8 bars: first remove the extra hat rolls and syncopations, then mute the hats completely while keeping kick, snare, 808, and pad. After a few bars, begin filtering down the 808 and pad, shortening 808 decays and dulling the high end of the pad so the motif feels like it’s sinking underwater. Optionally drop the snare in the final 2 bars, leaving only a muffled 808 pulse and faint pad before cutting the 808 and letting the pad fade alone, ending cold and unresolved.)

name: pop
style: Instrumental-only melodic pop at 110 BPM in A minor with a bittersweet yet gently hopeful tone, centered on an expressive clean electric guitar lead over smooth bass and tight, steady drums. A flowing mid‑tempo backbeat with unobtrusive 8th‑note hats or shaker and only light fills keeps the groove constant and non‑aggressive. Warm, rounded bass locks to the kick on mostly root-based, stepwise motion, adding a bit more in hooks and simplifying in intro and bridge while never becoming a riff lead. The main clean guitar sits clearly on top with bright but smooth tone and vocal-like, singable motifs; verses stay more open, while hooks use a memorable repeating motif that defines the track’s identity. A secondary clean guitar quietly supports rhythm and harmony, a soft pad holds long background chords, and a delicate high‑texture synth or bell adds sparse hook-only accents, all kept under the lead within a polished Taylor-adjacent pop feel and clear space for an imagined vocal.
section:
[Intro]
(Lean atmospheric intro: soft synth pad holds gentle A minor chords while a secondary clean guitar plays very sparse, palm‑muted chord pulses. Drums enter after a moment with just kick and light closed hat, no full snare yet, and bass plays long root notes in A minor. The primary clean guitar introduces a short, understated motif that hints at the later hook, leaving space between phrases and riding the steady 110 BPM pulse.)
[Instrumental Verse 1]
(Bring in the full but still light backbeat: kick and crisp snare on 2 and 4, tight hats on 8ths. Bass locks with the kick on simple root‑based movement. Lead guitar plays relaxed, conversational motifs in mid register, slightly less catchy than the hook and leaving small gaps. Rhythm guitar stays low in the mix with muted 8th‑note chord pulses, and the pad remains a soft background wash. No high bell‑like synth yet, keeping dynamics medium and reflective.)
[Instrumental Hook 1]
(Lift the energy: drums brighten with slightly more open hats or gentle tambourine, while bass adds a few smooth passing tones to push forward. Lead guitar steps to the front with the main hook melody, a clear 4–8 bar motif that repeats with subtle end‑of‑phrase variations and expressive slides. Rhythm guitar widens in stereo with light double‑tracking but stays supportive. Introduce a sparse bell‑like synth layer for occasional high accents on downbeats or phrase endings, keeping the guitar clearly dominant.)
[Instrumental Bridge 1]
(Pull the density down without breaking the pulse: switch the snare to softer rim clicks and slightly thin the kick pattern, while bass holds longer notes with fewer passes. Lead guitar moves to more open, sustained phrases, exploring slightly different chord colors for a deeper bittersweet feel. Rhythm guitar shifts from tight pulses to airy, sustained voicings or drops out in spots, and the pad swells a little to carry emotional weight. Remove the bell‑like synth to keep this section introspective but still gently hopeful.)
[Instrumental Hook 2]
(Return to the full hook groove, now as the emotional peak. Drums regain the crisp backbeat and brighter hats/tambourine; bass is at its most flowing while still supportive. Lead guitar restates the main hook melody with a touch more expression—extra slides, occasional octave or simple harmony notes on key moments—without turning into a solo. Rhythm guitar is widest and most consistent here, filling the stereo field under the lead. Bell‑like synth accents are slightly more frequent than in Hook 1 yet remain sparse, keeping the texture polished and clear.)
[Outro]
(Gently wind down while keeping the steady groove: drop tambourine and slightly soften hats, then let the snare fall away in the final bars, leaving mostly kick and hat. Bass simplifies back to longer root notes. Lead guitar plays a pared‑down version of the hook, leaving more space until it ends on a tender held or sliding note. High bell synth disappears early; rhythm guitar and pad thin out so that a final clean guitar chord or soft pad chord in A minor (with a hopeful added 9) sustains the ending and lets the track fade or resolve quietly.)
